description: Login validation and access control: enforce NGO approval status at login, block pending/rejected NGOs from accessing dashboard, apply ngo_approved_required to relief routes. Depends on FEAT-003 (admin approval workflow).
steps: 1. Modify /login route in app.py. After successful password verification and before setting session, check if user.ngo_registration_id is not NULL. If not NULL: query ngo_registrations for that id, check status. If PENDING: flash 'Your NGO application is pending admin approval. You will be notified when approved.' with severity 'warning', do not set session, redirect to login. If REJECTED: flash 'Your NGO application was rejected. Reason: {rejection_reason}. Please contact support.' with severity 'error', redirect to login. If APPROVED: proceed to set session and login normally. If NULL (legacy relief users): proceed normally.

2. Add ngo_approved_required() decorator function in app.py after login_required(). Logic: @functools.wraps wrapper that checks if session['role'] == 'relief' AND user has ngo_registration_id, then verifies status == APPROVED in ngo_registrations table. If not approved: flash error, redirect to home_redirect(). This decorator ensures relief routes check both login AND approval status.
4. Keep /profile and /logout routes accessible to all authenticated users (do NOT add ngo_approved_required), so pending NGOs can still update profile or logout.

5. Test backward compatibility: existing relief users without ngo_registration_id should bypass NGO checks entirely. Pattern: in ngo_approved_required, check if user has ngo_registration_id first - if NULL, allow access (they're legacy users). Only check approval status if ngo_registration_id is not NULL.

6. Update /ngo/application-status route to detect if user is logged in and their application is pending/rejected, show personalized message: 'You are logged in but cannot access the dashboard until your application is approved.' vs 'Your application is under review.'

7. Add helper function get_ngo_status(user_id) in app.py that queries ngo_registrations by user.ngo_registration_id and returns status or None. Use this in ngo_approved_required and login route to avoid duplicate queries.
acceptance_criteria: NGOs with PENDING status cannot login, see appropriate message
NGOs with REJECTED status cannot login, see rejection reason
NGOs with APPROVED status login successfully to relief dashboard
Legacy relief users without ngo_registration_id login normally (backward compatible)
All relief routes protected by ngo_approved_required check approval status
Profile and logout remain accessible to pending NGOs if they somehow get session
Login page shows clear feedback for pending/rejected NGO applications
Application status page reflects logged-in user's state if applicable
verification: Create NGO registration (FEAT-002), do NOT approve it (status=PENDING)
Try to login with NGO email and password at /login with role=relief
Verify login blocked with message 'Your NGO application is pending admin approval'
Verify session not created, user redirected back to login
Login as admin, reject the NGO with reason 'Missing documents'
Try to login with rejected NGO credentials
Verify login blocked with message showing rejection reason
Login as admin, approve a different NGO (FEAT-003)
Try to login with approved NGO credentials
Verify login succeeds, redirects to relief user dashboard (/home)
Test backward compatibility: login as riverside@ngo.org/relief123 (legacy user with ngo_registration_id=NULL)
Verify login succeeds, all relief routes accessible
Check database to confirm riverside user has ngo_registration_id=NULL: sqlite3 reliefgrid.db 'SELECT ngo_registration_id FROM users WHERE email="riverside@ngo.org"'
Verify no errors in console during any of these login tests
